previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of neurogenic bladder, paraplegia, and recent pyelonephritis returned to the emergency department after eloping from the hospital less than 12 hours earlier. She presented with severe back pain, nausea, and tachycardia, which were attributed to cocaine use despite recent clinical improvement. She was treated with IV ceftriaxone and pain management, including a temporary groin central venous catheter for medication administration. Her condition stabilized, and she was transitioned to oral nitrofurantoin to complete her antibiotic course. Other medications were adjusted, including a reduced dose of amitriptyline and increased omeprazole. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up and monitor for recurrent symptoms.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo female with a history of pyeloneprhitis/UTI who is 
admitted with fevers and flank pain.

* ? UTI/pyeloneprhitis - Had a dirty UA in the ED prior to 
receiving antibiotics and was started on gentamicin.  Her last 
two UCx grew E coli sensative to CTX and nitrofurantoin and has 
a history of Enterococcus.  She was started on the floor on 
Vancomycin and CTX and remained afebrile.  Her Foley was 
replaced.  On the third hospital day, her urine culture grew 
multiple bacterial flora, suggestive of colonization.  Her blood 
cultures remained negative. Her antibiotics were discontinued 
and she was monitored for 24 hours off antibiotics.  She 
remained afebrile during her hospitalization and had no 
leukocytosis.  She may have a component of chronic pain, but did 
not feel her presentation was concerning for acute 
pyelonephritis.  She was treated supportively with good effect.

* R ___ toe laceration - She does not remember when she 
developed this laceration, but given her paraplegia, did not 
feel any pain.  An Xray was done which showed soft tissue 
swelling and no evidence of cortical bone destruction.  An 
ESR/CRP was drawn which were 14 and 8, respectively.  The 
podiatry team was called to assess if any further debridement or 
management was required.  The team felt that it was a 
non-infected superficial wound and would heal with supportive 
care.  The wound was dressed and a boot provided..

* Neurogenic bladder - Foley was removed and changed out on 
admission.  

* Substance abuse - On her most recent admission, she eloped and 
returned with a U tox positive for cocaine.  She refuses 
treatment programs at this time.

* Spasms - Continued amitryptyline and cyclobenzaprine

* Depression - Stable, no SI/HI.  Continued fluoxetine 40mg 
daily

* GERD - Continued prilosec 40mg daily

remained afebrile x 24 hours and were not sent home with 
antibiotics.  Your pain is likely related to muscle spasm.

FINDINGS:  Bandage material projecting over the fifth toe.  The cortical

degenerative changes at the level of the first, second, and fifth toe.
